project.name: waydroid-apps
project.description: Declarative, data-driven provisioning of a curated Android app set into the local Waydroid (LineageOS) container, plus seeding of the launcher hotseat ('bottom bar'). Apps are pinned in src/apps.lock.json (F-Droid suggestedVersionCode + nix-prefetched sha256), fetched reproducibly by src/flake.nix, installed with `waydroid app install`, and arranged in the dock from each app's `dock_order`. NOTHING is hardcoded in the engine: package list, dock order, F-Droid endpoints, Waydroid data roots and the launcher DB are all read from this file or discovered at runtime (the engine introspects the live `favorites` schema before writing — the DB filename is grid-dependent, e.g. launcher_6_by_5.db, so it is globbed, never assumed).

waydroid._doc: Host-side facts. data_roots is a candidate list; the engine picks the first that exists (multi-machine reproducible). launcher_package is the LineageOS Launcher3. launcher_db_glob is grid-dependent (launcher_<cols>_by_<rows>.db) so it MUST be globbed under the launcher's databases/ dir, never hardcoded. hotseat_container=-101 and item_type_application=0 are AOSP Launcher3 constants.

dock._doc: The hotseat has a fixed slot count derived from the launcher grid (6 on a 6_by_5 grid). Apps with a non-null dock_order are placed left-to-right by ascending dock_order (slot = dock_order - 1). Apps with dock_order=null are installed but live only in the app drawer. To re-arrange the bottom bar, edit dock_order values here and re-run `build.sh dock` — no code changes.
